title: He didn’t hear God that day.
paragraphs: He didn’t hear God that day.
No whisper. No vision. No dream.
Just silence… and a torn piece of fabric soaked in blood.

Jacob held Joseph’s coat in trembling hands, the one he had once given with pride, now returned with a lie stitched into every thread. The colors that once reflected favor now screamed loss. And in that moment, something inside him collapsed.
The Scripture says it plainly, but the weight of it is unbearable if you really sit in it:

“וַיַּכִּרָהּ וַיֹּאמֶר כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ טָרֹף טֹרַף יוֹסֵף”
Vayyakkirah vayomer: ketonet beni; chayyah ra’ah achalathu; tarof toraf Yosef
“Then he recognized it and said, ‘It is my son’s robe. A wild animal has devoured him. Joseph is without doubt torn to pieces.’” — Genesis 37:33
He believed it.
Not because it was true… but because it felt true.
And sometimes that’s the most dangerous kind of lie.
The kind that aligns perfectly with your worst fear.
The kind that requires no evidence because your heart is already breaking.
Jacob tore his garments. He put on sackcloth. He mourned for days that turned into years. And when people tried to comfort him, he refused.
“I will go down to Sheol to my son, mourning.” — Genesis 37:35

The Hebrew word used there for mourning, “אֵבֶל” (evel), isn’t casual grief. It’s deep, consuming sorrow. The kind that reshapes your identity. The kind that convinces you life will never feel whole again.
Jacob didn’t just lose Joseph…
He buried the future he thought God had promised.
Because Joseph had dreams.
God-given dreams.
Dreams where his brothers bowed… where his life had purpose… where something bigger was unfolding.
But now?
All Jacob could see was blood.
And maybe that’s where this hits harder than expected…
Because you’ve held your own “bloody coat” before.
Something you thought God gave you… something that felt sacred… something full of promise… now lying in pieces in your hands.
A relationship that died.
A prayer that went unanswered.
A future that never happened.
And the silence of God felt louder than the pain itself.
Be honest.
This hit deeper than you expected.
Because what hurts most isn’t just loss…
It’s the feeling that God allowed it.
Jacob didn’t know what heaven knew.
He didn’t see Joseph in the pit.
He didn’t see the Ishmaelites passing by.
He didn’t see the Midianite traders.
He didn’t see Egypt.
He didn’t see Potiphar.
He didn’t see the prison.
He didn’t see the palace.
He didn’t see the famine.
He didn’t see the reunion.
He didn’t see the tears that would one day wash away this grief.
He only saw the coat.
And he built his entire belief around incomplete evidence.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because heaven never confirmed Joseph was dead.
It only allowed Jacob to believe it.
And that changes everything.
Because sometimes God will allow a narrative to unfold that looks like loss… feels like death… and sounds like silence… but is actually positioning something far greater than you can comprehend.
Joseph wasn’t dead.
He was being developed.
The Hebrew root behind Joseph’s name, “יָסַף” (yasaf), means “to add,” “to increase,” “to continue doing again.”
Jacob thought God had taken something away.
But God was actually multiplying something unseen.
And maybe… just maybe…
That’s what’s happening in your life right now.
You’re grieving something God is still growing.
You’re burying something heaven is still building.
You’re calling it over… while God is calling it forward.
Because God doesn’t move through fake strength.
He meets you in honest surrender.
Years later, when Joseph finally revealed himself, the truth shattered the lie Jacob had lived with for so long.
Joseph said:

“וְעַתָּה לֹא אַתֶּם שְׁלַחְתֶּם אֹתִי הֵנָּה כִּי הָאֱלֹהִים”
Ve’atah lo atem shelachtem oti henah, ki ha’Elohim
“And now it was not you who sent me here, but God.” — Genesis 45:8
And then again:
“You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good.” — Genesis 50:20
The Hebrew word for “meant” there is “חָשַׁב” (chashav) — to weave, to plan, to think, to account.
God was weaving… while Jacob was weeping.
God was planning… while Jacob was mourning.
God was writing… while Jacob thought the story had ended.
And this is the truth most people don’t want to hear…
Just because it looks dead doesn’t mean God is done.
Just because you don’t understand it doesn’t mean He’s not in it.
Just because it hurts doesn’t mean it’s not holy.
Because healing isn’t always loud.
Sometimes it looks like survival.
Sometimes it looks like getting up when you don’t want to.
Sometimes it looks like holding on to God when everything in you wants to let go.
And if you’ve read this far, this isn’t random.
This is a moment.
A turning point.
A quiet invitation to stop believing the version of your story that pain has been telling you.
Because Jesus didn’t come just to comfort you…
He came to rewrite you.
The same God who allowed Jacob to sit in grief…
Is the same God who restored him with overwhelming joy.
The same God who allowed Joseph to be betrayed…
Is the same God who elevated him beyond imagination.
This is the Gospel.
Scandal to grace.
Brokenness to redemption.
Death to life.
And it all points to Jesus.
Because on a hill called Golgotha, it looked like another story had ended.
Blood was spilled.
Hope looked buried.
Silence filled the sky.
But heaven wasn’t finished.
The Greek word Jesus cried, “Τετέλεσται” (Tetelestai) — “It is finished” (John 19:30) — wasn’t defeat.
It was fulfillment.
It meant the debt was paid.
The story was complete.
The victory was secured.
And three days later… the stone rolled away.
Because what looks final on earth… is often just the beginning in heaven.
So before you walk away…
Sit with it.
Respond to it.
Because there are more people reading your comment than you realize… and your honesty might be the lifeline someone else needed.
And if you truly want to glorify God through your life, not just your words…
Support what is feeding your spirit.
This isn’t just content.
This is calling.
This is alignment.
This is choosing truth over comfort.
Because staying close to truth is how you survive seasons that try to break you.
And maybe the coat in your hands isn’t proof that it’s over…
Maybe it’s proof that you’re in the middle of a story God hasn’t finished yet.
